newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bangkok Bank sees no quick Thai rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Bangkok Bank sees no quick Thai rate cut.

text.p: The president of Bangkok Bank Plc said on Thursday he does not expect a cut in Thai lending rates despite higher liquidity in the Thai banking system in the past two days.

Bangkok Bank president Chartsiri Sophonpanich told reporters that rising money supply in the Thai money market since Tuesday is an aberration created by a sudden shift of deposits from finance companies to commercial banks in the wake of public concern over the stability of finance firms.

Market analysts said at least 15-20 billion baht ($581 million-$775 million) of public deposits have been transferred to banks from finance companies in the last few days after the Bank of Thailand instructed 10 cash-strapped finance firms to raise capital on Monday.
The central bank said the immediate capital hike would help convince creditors of these firms that they could continue to operate soundly.
The Thai overnight interbank rate eased to 7.00-7.50 percent late on Thursday from 15-20 percent in mid-February.

Bank treasury officials said the overnight rate for funds borrowed among finance companies hovered at 14-18 percent this week as most finance firms maintained contingency big cash reserves to meet withdrawals by jittery clients.

"Short-term interest rates need to stay stable at current levels for a little longer before we can get the real liquidity picture...interbank rates have to remain low for a relatively long time (before we cut lending rates)," Chartsiri said.
The banker said any move by the U.S. Federal Reserve Board to hike U.S. interest rates would delay Thai rate cuts.
